The decision summary composes steps 2 and

4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measuremen
tUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials ins
ide them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each — 3 aga
inst 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n across tha
t line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through
on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagn
ostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusi
ve`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconc
lusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the
whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n \"nothing failed\" from \"

we did not look".

ur **expected output** if you set one, and against the user prompt otherwise. It's advisory: it produces a score and a rationale,
but doesn't gate the run unless you ask it to.\n262:* When grading against the prompt rather than an expected output, scores are c
apped at 0.85 — you can't get a \"perfect\" without saying what perfect means.\n272:**Data sent for rubric checks:** when a suite
has grading criteria or rubric-check questions, every trial the goal-completion judge grades is also sent to TypeSafe AI's Jev cla
ssifier through Vercel AI Gateway: the request, the expected outcome, the final answer and a clipped trajectory, with credentials
redacted. If Jev can't be reached, the same questions go to a fallback model through Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter. Turn rubric
checks off in suite settings if that isn't appropriate for your data.\n638:Click a **test case name** to open its definition — the

s (passed count, P50, P95, tokens, calls) and a flat iteration list. Click an iteration row to open its full detail view — scoreca
rd, transcript, tool calls, and trace — without leaving the run page. A **Back** breadcrumb returns to the iteration list. In the
scorecard, each evaluator row shows an **Expected** field (the configured criterion) and an **Actual** field (what the run recorde
d). When the findings pipeline has produced a narrative for the iteration, the **Actual** field shows the AI-generated explanation
; if the narrative predates the latest grade it is marked stale and the recorded evidence is shown instead. Evaluators are grouped
by stage rather than split into default and added-assertion sections.\n644: * **Missing** — expected tool calls that were never

# Create an eval suite (author-only, does not run)

> Creates a runnable eval suite — the suite record plus
its test cases — and responds `201` **synchronously**, WITHOUT executing anything. Use this to author a suite, then run it later w
ith `POST /eval-runs` (passing the returned `suiteId`).\n\nThis is distinct from `POST /eval-runs`, which creates a run and **deta
ches execution**, responding `202` with a `runId`. There is no concurrency cap here (no run is started).\n\nThe body uses an ergon
omic authoring shape: a suite-level default `model` (and optional `provider`) applies to every test unless the test overrides it;
`provider` is derived from a `provider/model` id when neither is supplied. Each test's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prom

pt / toolCall / interact / assert).

Guest callers are denied (suite creation is a write).
